subject.title: Memory compaction blocks main processing lane, causing unresponsive bot for 10+ minutes

question: Should OpenClaw isolate or preempt compaction and memoryFlush work from foreground same-session message handling, and what transcript-ordering contract should that design preserve?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the fix is a scheduler/session-state design choice rather than a narrow line repair because it changes how compaction, memoryFlush, transcript rotation, active-run steering, and channel acknowledgments interact.

options.title: Design a bounded maintenance lane
options.body: Move compaction and memoryFlush to a dedicated bounded/preemptible maintenance path with explicit ordering and recovery tests for foreground channel messages.

options.title: Keep serialization and add busy recovery
options.body: Keep the current same-lane model but add a shorter bounded failure path plus visible busy/retry recovery so users are not silently blocked.

options.title: Preserve blocking behavior
options.body: Treat compaction as intentionally foreground and close or defer nonblocking message handling as out of scope for now.

recommendation.title: Design a bounded maintenance lane
recommendation.body: Move compaction and memoryFlush to a dedicated bounded/preemptible maintenance path with explicit ordering and recovery tests for foreground channel messages.
